title: One UWB Radar, Many Views: Comparing and Fusing Signal Representations for Human Activity Recognition
abstract: arXiv:2611.30033v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: IEEE 802.15.4z-compliant impulse-radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) transceivers are increasingly built into consumer devices, enabling contactless, privacy-preserving human activity recognition (HAR) in healthcare. Before activity classification, the signal is typically converted into range-time, range-Doppler, or time-Doppler maps, each exposing different spatial and motion cues. Existing comparisons often apply shared processing across representations, leaving it unclear whether their rankings hold after independent tuning. It is also unknown whether rankings and fusion gains generalize across environments and activities, and at what computational cost. Consequently, practitioners lack guidance on which representation and processing suit a given HAR deployment. We release an open dataset of raw IR-UWB measurements collected by a ceiling-mounted radar from 44 participants during scripted activity sequences in 12 layouts across two bedroom

translated_title: 单一UWB雷达，多种视角：面向人体活动识别的信号表示比较与融合
translated_abstract: 符合IEEE 802.15.4z标准的脉冲无线电超宽带收发器正日益被集成到消费设备中，从而在医疗保健领域实现非接触式、保护隐私的人体活动识别（HAR）。在进行活动分类之前，信号通常会被转换为距离-时间图、距离-多普勒图或时间-多普勒图，每种图各自展现不同的空间与运动线索。现有的比较研究往往在不同信号表示上套用共享的处理流程，因此尚不清楚在独立调优后各表示的性能排名是否仍然成立。此外，这些排名与融合收益能否跨环境和跨活动泛化，以及其计算代价如何，也尚属未知。因此，从业者在为特定HAR部署选择合适的信号表示与处理方法时缺乏指导。我们发布了一个开源的原始IR-UWB测量数据集，由吸顶式雷达采集，涵盖44名参与者在两个卧室的12种布局中按预设脚本进行的活动序列……
tldr: 本文发布了一个由吸顶式UWB雷达采集的原始开源数据集（44名参与者、两个卧室的12种布局），并对距离-时间、距离-多普勒和时间-多普勒三种信号表示在独立调优下的人体活动识别性能、跨环境泛化能力、融合收益及计算成本进行了系统比较，为实际HAR部署中的信号表示选择提供了指导。
en_tdlr: This paper releases an open raw IR-UWB dataset collected by a ceiling-mounted radar (44 participants, 12 layouts across two bedrooms) and systematically compares and fuses range-time, range-Doppler, and time-Doppler representations for human activity recognition under independent tuning, providing practical guidance on representation selection and computational cost for real-world HAR deployments.
